newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bureaucracy keeps on growing-Comptroller.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bureaucracy keeps on growing-Comptroller.

text.p: Despite moves to decentralize public services, Venezuela's central state bureaucracy continues to grow and is increasingly inefficient, a top ranking public official said Monday.

"There is a strong contradiction between the public discourse about decentralization and the fact that the state keeps on growing," Filippo Vagoni, a director of the Comptroller General's Office, was quoted as saying in a release.
As an example, he pointed to the Transport and Communications Ministry which in spite of the creation of autonomous regional transport bodies, had not reduced its payroll.
According to Vagoni, there are currently 1,700 separate entities in the Venezuelan public sector which receive public funds.

Vagoni also highlighted the excessive rotation of public officials, "which leads to plans and projects not being finished," and questioned the huge stocks of out-of-date medicines in public hospitals and the lack of materials to produce compulsory identity papers and passports.

The Comptroller General's Office, the top watchdog on the way public funds are spent and administered, frequently exposes and criticizes corruption and inefficiency in the public sector. But its reports and statements rarely lead to any concrete changes.
